Name: Dallas Buyers Club
Review:
This movie made me like Matthew McConaughey.

Going into this film I was expecting nothing. The journey you take with Ron through the trials he faces as a newly stricken victim of HIV is not heartbreaking, but sad and not in the way you'd expect.

I didn't come out of this movie really liking Ron. I say, don't be fooled by the outer image of him being the hero and helping others with HIV; his motivations are solely greed.  It's not until he loses Rayon (Leto) that any real care for others shines through. Ron, like most of the other characters, is in it for himself. 

This is 'based on a true story', and knowing that writers twist stories to entertain, I was still enthralled. Great movie with some of the best performances of Leto and McConaughy I've seen.

Name: The Wolf of Wall Street
Review:
Hard movie to review. What should have been a great time at the movies, left me feeling disgusted. This movie makes me cringe when I think about how it's nothing more than Hollywood telling an audience that it's wrong to be like Jordan, but the entire time Hollywood is proving they do not practice what they preach. We are shown a man that uses and abuses anyone to get to the top. We are shown how it is wrong. In the end nothing bad happens to Jordan. He still receives his money and only does light time. 

If I watch this movie blind to the hypocrisy, then it's a fun film full of crazy antics. I always enjoy DiCaprio, but I wish that he would have opted out of this piece.
